question: Why Is Chick-fil-A Closed on Sunday?
quick_answer: Chick-fil-A is closed every Sunday because founder S. Truett Cathy set it as a day of rest from the very beginning. He wanted employees to have a guaranteed day off to rest and spend time with family, tied to his own faith, and the company has kept the policy ever since. Almost every Chick-fil-A in the US stays closed on Sundays.
key_facts: A policy set by founder S. Truett Cathy from day one in 1967
Meant to give employees a guaranteed day of rest
Tied to the founder's Christian faith
Still company policy today across the US

body.heading: A rule from the founder
body.text: Chick-fil-A has been closed on Sundays since founder S. Truett Cathy opened his first restaurant. He decided early on that his restaurants would not open on Sundays, and that choice became a permanent part of how the company operates.

body.heading: Rest and faith
body.text: The main reasons are rest and faith. Cathy wanted every employee to have at least one guaranteed day off each week to rest, be with family, and worship if they chose to. The decision was rooted in his own Christian beliefs, and the company has described it as a way of valuing people over extra sales.

body.heading: Does it ever open on Sunday?
body.text: As a rule, no. The vast majority of Chick-fil-A locations stay closed every Sunday. There are a small number of unusual exceptions, such as certain locations inside airports or stadiums that are operated differently, but the standard across the chain is closed on Sundays.

faqs.q: Is every Chick-fil-A closed on Sunday?
faqs.a: Almost all of them. The standard company policy is to close on Sundays. A few unusual locations, such as some in airports or stadiums, can differ, but the normal rule is closed.

faqs.q: Who decided Chick-fil-A would close on Sundays?
faqs.a: Founder S. Truett Cathy made the decision from the start, so employees would have a guaranteed day of rest. It was tied to his Christian faith.

faqs.q: Does Chick-fil-A lose money by closing on Sundays?
faqs.a: It gives up a day of potential sales, but the company has kept the policy for decades, saying the day of rest for staff matters more than the extra revenue.
